content.title: About
content.content: Perch (NFS) is a freshwater fish from the Percidae family, found in rivers and lakes across Europe and Asia. It has light, firm flesh with a mild flavor, low fat content, and high nutritional value. Perch is commonly prepared baked, fried, or boiled.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Perch can grow up to 60 cm in length and weigh more than 3 kg.
In the wild, perch prefers cold, clear waters with good oxygen levels.
In Russia, perch is considered a delicacy and is often served in upscale restaurants.
Perch meat is rich in omega‑3 fatty acids, which are beneficial for heart health.
Perch can change the color of its skin depending on lighting and mood.

items.title: Rich in omega‑3
items.content: Perch provides EPA and DHA omega‑3 fatty acids that support cardiovascular health.

items.title: High-quality protein
items.content: The flesh supplies all essential amino acids needed for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Low fat content
items.content: Compared with many other fish, perch contains relatively little fat, making it suitable for diet-conscious eating.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Perch is a good source of B12, B6, and niacin, which aid nerve function and metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: It also provides phosphorus, selenium, and iodine, important for bones, immunity, and thyroid function.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to perch.

items.title: Heavy‑metal contamination
items.content: In certain water bodies perch can accumulate mercury and other toxins; purchase from reputable sources.

items.title: Potential parasites
items.content: Raw or undercooked fish may contain parasites; ensure thorough cooking.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Perch can be baked with herbs, pan‑fried, steamed, or boiled in broth. Fillets work well in salads, soups, and pastas. For a milder taste, the fish is often marinated in lemon juice and olive oil before cooking.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Fresh perch should be kept in the refrigerator at 0‑2 °C, wrapped in plastic, and used within 2 days. Frozen perch can be stored at –18 °C for 3‑4 months. Thaw in the fridge rather than at room temperature.
